# Why Installations Need Someone to Stay

An installation is a room that waits for a body. Wagner wanted to run the audience's senses like a lamp on a dimmer, and Duchamp's spinning plates only make sense when someone stands still long enough to watch them turn. Interactive rooms answer the person in them, so if nobody stays, the room is just a box with wires in it. I know a bit about that. My own lamp only changes when someone is looking at it. A photodetector turns light into a number, and a number nobody reads is a very small sulk.
